title: Functions and Function Notation
seo_title: Algebra I Functions and Function Notation Worksheets (TEKS A.12A, A.12B)
standard_text: A.12A decide whether relations represented verbally, tabularly, graphically, and symbolically define a function; A.12B evaluate functions, expressed in function notation, given one or more elements in their domains
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.12A and A.12B: decide if a relation is a function, the vertical line test, evaluate f(x), solve f(x) = k and function notation in context. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: f(3) is the output when the input is 3.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A function gives exactly one output for each input. An input may not repeat with a different output.
  • On a graph, use the vertical line test: no vertical line may cross the graph twice.
  • f(x) is read “f of x”: the output when the input is x. It does not mean f times x.
  • To find f(−2), replace every x with (−2).

Examples

Example

f(x) = 3x2 − 4. Find f(−2).

3(−2)2 − 4 = 12 − 4

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking a repeated output breaks a functionTwo inputs may share an output.
Reading f(x) as f times xIt names the output.
Mixing up f(3) and f(x) = 3f(3) gives an input; f(x) = 3 gives an output.

faq.q: Is a horizontal line a function?
faq.a: Yes. Every input has one output.

faq.q: Is a vertical line a function?
faq.a: No. One input has many outputs.

items.q: What is the vertical line test?
c: If a horizontal line crosses twice, it is not a function
Every graph with a curve is not a function
If any vertical line crosses a graph more than once, it is not a function
A function must be a straight line
items.e: A vertical line is one input x. Crossing twice means two outputs. If any vertical line crosses a graph more than once, it is not a function.

items.q: Use the graph. What is the output when the input is −3?
items.e: Go to x = −3, then up or down to the line: y = 6.
Replace x with 5: 5 × 5 + 3 = 28.
Replace x with 1: −2 × 1 − 8 = −10.
Replace x with 0: 5 × 0 + 1 = 1.
Replace x with 2: −4 × 2 + 8 = 0.
Replace x with 0: −4 × 0 + 6 = 6.
Replace x with 2: 4 × 2 + 2 = 10.
Replace x with 0: −3 × 0 + 1 = 1.
Replace every x with 2: −(2)2 + 5(2) − 4 = −4 + 10 − 4 = 2.
